trustRules: All target item names, numbers, slot icons, attributes, statuses and class identities are placeholders; the eight retained regions and fixed-density workbench composition are authoritative.
The editable loadout starts from equippedSet only. An empty equippedSet remains empty and must not be synthesized from slotReadiness, replacementCandidates or the first community template.
The route uses compact mode only as a lightweight candidate catalog; compact readiness aggregates catalog candidates and is never editable-state truth.
The catalog bootstrap omits mode=initial because that backend mode intentionally returns slot shells with empty item arrays; mode=slot is reserved for on-demand details.

Candidate identity, item level, stats, compatibility and source render only when returned for that candidate. In compact slot mode, socketOptions, enchantOptions and embellishmentOptions are group-owned sets projected onto each exact item while item.modCapabilities remains item-owned.

Only enhancement options with a backend id or optionKey are selectable. Missing canonical identity is filtered and leaves the requested enhancement group blocked; Taro never fabricates option-N identifiers.

Candidate click -> local draft only; apply / confirm -> gearResolve -> verified resolvedSlots proof -> committed UI. Candidate apply requires exact resolved itemId + variantKey identity and both candidate/enhancement commits materialize confirmed selectedOptions through the domain snapshot helper. Request intent, local draft and snapshot.selectionIntent are never success proof.

Variant-scoped craftedStatOptions without a resolver-owned identifier are display only after that variant is selected; object simcOptions expose only safely formatted scalar display values and no selectable action or craftedOptionId.
Only HTTPS item or enhancement media on the explicit trusted runtime allowlist may render as real WoW objects; generated or decorative art cannot impersonate an item.

Resolver readiness remains backend-owned for deterministic save metadata: an initial equippedSet may use websim.gear.readiness only when its selectedCount matches the editable selection; every edited draft uses gearResolve.profileReadiness. Taro never counts item simcReady flags or hardcodes a 15-slot rule; candidate counts are never presented as equipped counts.

The loadout summary exposes only the current item level and backend-derived attribute values. Its fixed visual order is primary/stamina first, haste/critical/mastery/versatility on the left, and leech/avoidance/speed on the right; every attribute row uses the left-column row height, so the unused lower-right cell remains empty. Missing backend fields retain their position as 未提供 or 待校验. It does not expose selected-count or readiness-state copy, readiness count, progress percentage or readiness checkpoints.

Community gear may be imported only from a returned template containing real gearItems and a verified hero-slot projection (heroKey, talentWinnerId and gearProjectionMode); it reuses the corresponding talent-source player and is identified as a source template, not BiS or an official recommendation. A gear-only fallback may use only the next legal candidate in the same class/spec/hero sequence and never changes the talent winner.

Save persists the complete current gearBySlot plus enhancementBySlot draft. Import always asks for one source group and then one exact template; reset clears all currently equipped slots, enhancements, candidate state and derived validation state instead of restoring equippedSet.

Loading, empty, blocked, stale and error states retain all eight regions, sixteen slot rows in two equal-width auto-fill columns and three fixed action positions; the internal candidate surface remains the only scrollable area.
